examples.ko: 아이가 좋은 일이 생겼다고 오두방정을 떨어요.
examples.en: The child is making a big fuss because something good happened.

examples.ko: 그렇게 오두방정 떨지 말고 차분히 말해 봐요.
examples.en: Stop making such a fuss and tell me calmly.

examples.ko: 동생이 시험에 붙고 하루 종일 오두방정을 떨었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling passed the exam and acted giddy all day.

examples.ko: 오두방정 좀 그만 떨고 얼른 앉아요.
examples.en: Quit fussing around and sit down quickly.
The puppy goes wild when it sees a guest.

examples.ko: 별일도 아닌데 왜 그렇게 오두방정을 떠는지 모르겠어요.
examples.en: It's nothing special, so I don't know why you're making such a fuss.

explain: '호들갑'과 비슷하게 가볍고 경솔하게 떠드는 모습에 써요. 거의 '오두방정을 떨다'로만 나오고, 보통 못마땅하거나 장난스럽게 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '호들갑' and describes acting light, rash and noisy. It almost always appears as '오두방정을 떨다', usually with a disapproving or teasing tone.

examples.ko: 길가에서 강아지 한 마리가 오들오들 떨고 있었어요.
examples.en: A puppy was shivering by the roadside.

examples.ko: 겨울인데 외투도 없이 나가서 오들오들 떨었어요.
examples.en: It's winter and I went out without a coat, so I shivered.

examples.ko: 비를 맞은 아이가 입술이 파래져서 오들오들 떨어요.
examples.en: The child who got caught in the rain has blue lips and is trembling.

examples.ko: 난방이 꺼진 방에서 오들오들 떨면서 잤어요.
examples.en: I slept shivering in a room with the heating off.

examples.ko: 무서운 영화를 보고 오들오들 떨던 친구가 생각나요.
examples.en: I remember my friend who trembled after watching a scary movie.

examples.ko: 왜 그렇게 오들오들 떨어요? 추우면 이불 덮어요.
examples.en: Why are you shivering like that? If you're cold, cover up with a blanket.

explain: 추위나 무서움 때문에 몸을 작게 계속 떠는 모습이에요. 거의 '떨다'와 함께 쓰고, 추울 때뿐 아니라 겁이 날 때도 써요.
explain_en: It shows a body trembling in small, continuous shakes from cold or fear. It almost always goes with '떨다' and works for fear as well as cold.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 코가 오뚝해서 인상이 또렷해요.
examples.en: That actor has a well-defined nose, so his look is striking.

examples.ko: 코가 오뚝한 사람이 부럽다고 친구가 말했어요.
examples.en: My friend said she envies people with high-bridged noses.
My older sister has a high nose bridge and big eyes.

examples.ko: 아기 코가 아직 오뚝하지 않아도 귀여워요.
examples.en: The baby's nose isn't high yet, but it's still cute.

examples.ko: 오뚝한 코를 가진 모델이 광고에 나와요.
examples.en: A model with a high-bridged nose appears in the ad.
I wish my nose were higher and sharper.

explain: 주로 코가 반듯하게 솟은 모양에 써요. '코가 높다'보다 보기 좋다는 느낌이 있어서 외모를 칭찬할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for a nose that rises neatly and sharply. Compared with '코가 높다', it carries a positive feel, so it suits compliments about looks.

examples.en: I sorted the names in ascending order in Excel.
If you line up the numbers in ascending order, it goes 1, 2, 3.
Shall we look at the scores in ascending or descending order?
Please organize the files by date in ascending order.
Try setting it so prices show in ascending order.
Please change it to descending instead of ascending.

explain: 반대말은 '내림차순'이에요. 엑셀이나 쇼핑 사이트에서 '정렬'과 함께 자주 나오고, 보통 '오름차순으로'의 형태로 써요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '내림차순' (descending order). It often appears with '정렬' (sorting) in Excel or shopping sites, usually in the form '오름차순으로'.

examples.ko: 이번 달 물가 오름폭이 지난달보다 커졌어요.
examples.en: This month's price increase is bigger than last month's.

examples.ko: 집값 오름폭이 조금 줄었다는 뉴스가 나왔어요.
examples.en: There was news that the rise in housing prices has slowed a little.
The rise in the stock price wasn't as big as I expected.

examples.ko: 기온 오름폭이 커서 옷 입기가 힘들어요.
examples.en: The temperature rises so much that it's hard to decide what to wear.

examples.ko: 전기 요금 오름폭이 얼마나 될지 궁금해요.
examples.en: I wonder how much electricity rates will go up.
The raise in my salary this year is small, so I'm disappointed.

explain: 물가, 집값, 금리처럼 숫자가 오른 정도를 말할 때 쓰고, '오름폭이 크다/줄다'로 자주 말해요. '상승폭'과 같은 뜻이고, 반대는 '하락폭'이에요.
explain_en: It is used for how much numbers such as prices, housing costs or interest rates went up, as in '오름폭이 크다/줄다'. It means the same as '상승폭', and its opposite is '하락폭'.

en: being foggy; being in the dark

examples.en: The cause of the accident is still a mystery.
I'm frustrated because there's no clue where the culprit went.
It's totally unclear what will happen to the company.
The whereabouts of the lost wallet were unknown.

examples.ko: 선거 결과가 오리무중이라 아무도 예상하지 못해요.
examples.en: The election result is so uncertain that nobody can predict it.
The plans keep changing, so I'm completely in the dark about the work.

explain: 거의 '오리무중이다'의 형태로, 상황이나 행방, 결과를 전혀 알 수 없을 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '감이 안 잡혀요'처럼 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It almost always appears as '오리무중이다' when a situation, whereabouts or result is impossible to know. In casual talk people also say '감이 안 잡혀요'.

examples.en: I scrunched up my face after eating something spicy.

examples.ko: 아침부터 오만상을 찌푸리고 있어요? 무슨 일 있어요?
examples.en: Why are you scowling since this morning? Did something happen?
The smell was so bad that everyone made a sour face.
Don't scowl; talk with a smile.
He grimaced when he saw his test score.

examples.ko: 사진 찍을 때 오만상을 찌푸리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't scowl when you take a photo.

explain: '인상을 쓰다'와 비슷한 상황에서 쓰는데, 얼굴을 한껏 찡그린 모습을 강조해요. 보통 '오만상을 찌푸리다'로 말하고 표정에만 써요.
explain_en: It is used in situations similar to '인상을 쓰다' but stresses a face scrunched up a lot. It usually appears as '오만상을 찌푸리다' and is only used for facial expressions.

examples.ko: 그는 군대 간 아들을 오매불망 기다렸어요.
examples.en: He waited longingly for his son who was in the army.

examples.ko: 팬들이 새 앨범을 오매불망 기다리고 있어요.
examples.en: Fans are eagerly waiting for the new album day and night.

examples.ko: 오매불망 바라던 합격 소식을 드디어 들었어요.
examples.en: I finally heard the news of passing that I had longed for.
My grandmother keeps longing for news from her hometown.
Today I met the family I had been dying to see.
The trip I've been waiting for so eagerly starts tomorrow.

explain: '기다리다, 그리워하다, 바라다' 같은 말과 자주 함께 써요. 조금 글 같은 표현이라 대화에서는 '애타게'가 더 편하게 들려요.
explain_en: It often goes with verbs like '기다리다', '그리워하다' and '바라다'. It sounds a bit literary, so in conversation '애타게' feels more casual.

examples.en: The baby eats baby food, working its mouth.
The hamster nibbles on a sunflower seed.
Grandmother said something, moving her lips.
The child put candy in its mouth and rolled it around.
The way the rabbit nibbles on grass is cute.

examples.ko: 입안에서 오물거리지 말고 크게 말해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't mumble in your mouth; speak up.

explain: 작은 입을 계속 움직이며 씹거나 말할 때 써서 귀엽고 작은 느낌이 있어요. '우물거리다'도 비슷하지만 더 크고 불분명하게 움직이는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used when a small mouth keeps moving as it chews or talks, with a cute, small feel. '우물거리다' is similar but feels bigger and less clear.

examples.en: The baby munches its food in small bites.
The rabbit is nibbling on a carrot.
I put candy in my mouth and rolled it around.

examples.ko: 아이가 오물오물 뭔가 말했는데 잘 안 들렸어요.
examples.en: The child mumbled something, but I couldn't hear it well.
The goldfish keeps moving its mouth.
Grandmother smiled while chewing slowly.

explain: '오물거리다'의 부사형으로, 작은 입이 계속 움직이는 모습을 말해요. '냠냠'처럼 소리를 흉내 내는 말이 아니라 입 모양이나 움직임을 보여 줘요.
explain_en: It is the adverb form of '오물거리다' and shows a small mouth moving continuously. Unlike '냠냠', it does not imitate a sound but describes the mouth's movement.

examples.en: Purse your lips and try whistling.
I cupped my hands and scooped up stream water to drink.
The baby curled its fingers and then opened them.
He was embarrassed and pursed his mouth.
The flower closes up its petals in the evening.
If you sit with your legs together, there's enough room.

explain: 반대말은 '벌리다'나 '펴다'예요. 입, 손, 꽃잎, 다리처럼 벌어진 것을 안쪽으로 모을 때 써요. 스스로 줄어드는 건 '오므라들다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Its opposites are '벌리다' and '펴다'. It is used when you draw something open, like a mouth, hand, petals or legs, inward. For something that shrinks on its own, use '오므라들다'.

examples.en: Small houses are huddled neatly together.

examples.ko: 하천 건너편은 오밀조밀 붙은 지붕들이 마치 장난감 마을 같았어요.
examples.en: The other side of the stream, with its snugly packed roofs, looked like a toy village.
Shops are packed closely along the alley.

examples.ko: 책상 위에 소품을 오밀조밀 꾸며 놓았어요.
examples.en: I arranged small items neatly on my desk.

examples.ko: 과일이 상자 안에 오밀조밀 담겨 있어요.
examples.en: The fruit is packed snugly in the box.

examples.ko: 동네가 오밀조밀 붙어 있어서 걸어 다니기 좋아요.
examples.en: The neighborhood is compact, so it's nice to get around on foot.

explain: 작은 것들이 촘촘하고 아기자기하게 모여 있는 모습에 써요. 답답하다기보다 정돈되고 귀여운 느낌으로 말할 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It describes small things gathered closely in a neat, charming way. It often feels tidy and cute rather than stuffy.

examples.ko: 소인국처럼 오밀조밀한 도시가 강 건너에 보였어요.
examples.en: A neat, tightly packed city like a tiny kingdom could be seen across the river.
This room is small but nicely compact, so it's cozy.
I like walking through the snug little alleys.
The inside of the shop is decorated in a neat, compact way.
That painter draws with delicate, close detail.

examples.ko: 집이 오밀조밀하지만 필요한 건 다 있어요.
examples.en: The house is compact, but it has everything you need.

explain: 공간이나 물건, 그림이 작고 촘촘하지만 짜임새 있을 때 써요. 단순히 '좁다'가 아니라 아기자기하게 잘 모여 있다는 좋은 느낌이 들어 있어요.
explain_en: It is used for spaces, objects or drawings that are small and dense yet well put together. It is not just 'narrow'; it carries a positive sense of being neatly arranged.

en: dead of night; middle of the night

examples.ko: 오밤중에 갑자기 전화가 와서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A phone call came in the dead of night and I was startled.
I want to eat ramyeon in the middle of the night.
Where are you going at this hour of the night?
It was noisy until the dead of night, so I couldn't sleep.
The child woke up in the middle of the night and cried.
It's the dead of night, so the buses have stopped running.

explain: '한밤중'과 같은 시간이지만 입말 느낌이 강해요. 늦은 시간에 놀랍거나 못마땅할 때 '이 오밤중에'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the same time as '한밤중' but sounds more colloquial. People often use it as '이 오밤중에' when surprised or annoyed at the late hour.

examples.en: Fireworks decorated the night sky in dazzling colors.
Brilliantly colored hanbok were hanging in the market.
The Christmas tree is so colorful it dazzles my eyes.
I walked through a field of multicolored flowers.
The stage lights changed into a rainbow of colors.
The autumn mountains are a blaze of color because of the leaves.

explain: 여러 가지 색이 화려하게 어우러진 모습에 써요. '알록달록'은 귀엽고 가벼운 느낌이고, '오색찬란'은 더 화려하고 멋진 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes many colors blending in a splendid way. '알록달록' feels cute and light, while '오색찬란' feels more gorgeous and grand.

examples.en: I tried drawing notes on staff paper.
The teacher drew a staff on the blackboard.
The composer wrote a melody on the staff paper.
I didn't have staff paper, so I drew lines in my notebook.
I bought a new book of staff paper.
Try copying the song onto staff paper.

explain: '악보'와 달리 음표를 적기 전의 줄만 그어진 종이를 말해요. 음악 시간이나 작곡 이야기에서 나오고, 비유로 '오선지 위의 음악'처럼도 써요.
explain_en: Unlike '악보' (sheet music), it refers to paper with just the five lines, before notes are written. It appears in music class or composing talk.

examples.en: I walked slowly along a path in the woods.
There is a small trail behind my house.
Wildflowers are blooming on both sides of the path.
If you follow the trail, you will reach a lake.

examples.ko: 좁은 오솔길이라 한 줄로 걸어야 해요.
examples.en: It's a narrow path, so we have to walk in a single line.
It rained earlier, so the trail is slippery.

explain: '산책로'와 달리 사람들이 오가며 저절로 생긴 듯한 좁은 길 느낌이에요. 주로 숲이나 산, 시골길에 쓰고, 소설이나 노래에서도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Unlike '산책로' (walking path), it suggests a narrow track that seems to have formed from people walking. It is mostly used for forests, mountains and country roads, and also appears in stories and songs.

examples.en: The family gathers cozily and eats dinner.
The old couple chats warmly together.

examples.ko: 친구들과 오순도순 사는 게 제 꿈이에요.
examples.en: My dream is to live peacefully with my friends.
The brothers get along so well, which is nice to see.
The neighbors live sharing warm feelings with each other.
Let's get along nicely.

explain: 사이좋게 정답게 모여 지내거나 이야기하는 모습에 써요. 주로 가족, 이웃, 친구처럼 가까운 사람들에게 쓰고, 보통 '지내다, 살다, 이야기하다'와 함께 나와요.
explain_en: It describes people getting along warmly, whether living together or talking. It is mostly used for close people like family, neighbors and friends, and usually goes with '지내다', '살다' and '이야기하다'.

examples.en: I may have a cold; I feel chilly all over.
The night wind was cold and I got goosebumps.
I might be getting a fever; I'm shivering a little.
I got rained on and now I feel chills.
I felt shivery cold, so I put a blanket over me.

examples.ko: 아침부터 오슬오슬 추운 게 감기 같아요.
examples.en: Feeling chilly since morning seems like a cold.

explain: 감기나 몸살 기운이 있을 때 으스스하게 추운 느낌에 많이 써요. '오들오들'은 몸을 떠는 모습이 더 크게 보이고, '오슬오슬'은 몸이 서늘해지는 느낌에 가까워요.
explain_en: It is often used for the creepy, shivery cold you feel when coming down with a cold or flu. '오들오들' emphasizes visible trembling, while '오슬오슬' is closer to the feeling of a chill passing through the body.

examples.en: My mother goes to the hospital because of frozen shoulder.

examples.ko: 오십견이 와서 팔을 위로 올리기 힘들어요.
examples.en: I have frozen shoulder, so it's hard to lift my arm up.
My father is getting treatment for frozen shoulder.

examples.ko: 오십견이 있으면 밤에 자다가 아플 수 있어요.
examples.en: With frozen shoulder, it can hurt while you sleep at night.
My shoulder hurts these days, and I'm worried it's frozen shoulder.
Light stretching helps with frozen shoulder.

explain: 이름에 '오십'이 들어가지만 꼭 오십 대에만 생기는 병은 아니에요. 보통 '오십견이 오다'나 '오십견이 있다'처럼 말하고, 어깨가 굳고 아픈 증상을 가리켜요.
explain_en: Though the name includes 'fifty', it does not only occur in people in their fifties. People usually say '오십견이 오다' or '오십견이 있다', referring to a stiff, painful shoulder.

en: being nearly the same; being six of one and a half dozen of the other

examples.en: Both scores are similar, so it's six of one, half a dozen of the other.

examples.ko: 그 가게나 이 가게나 가격은 오십보백보예요.
examples.en: That store and this store are about the same in price.

examples.ko: 내가 더 낫다고 해 봐야 오십보백보예요.
examples.en: Even if I say I'm better, it's about the same either way.
They're basically the same, so it doesn't matter which you pick.

examples.ko: 두 후보의 공약이 오십보백보라는 말이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people say the two candidates' pledges are no different.
They're about the same, so why argue so much?

explain: 둘 사이에 큰 차이가 없다고 말할 때 써요. '도토리 키 재기'나 '그게 그거예요'도 비슷한 표현이에요. 둘 다 부족한데 누가 낫다고 따질 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is used when there is no real difference between two things. '도토리 키 재기' and '그게 그거예요' are similar expressions. It often comes up when two flawed options are compared.

examples.en: My mother sobbed uncontrollably when she heard the news.
The audience sobbed in the last scene of the movie.

examples.ko: 그는 슬픈 소식을 듣고 오열하며 전화를 끊었어요.
examples.en: He hung up the phone, sobbing at the sad news.

examples.ko: 주인공이 오열하는 장면이 오래 기억에 남아요.
examples.en: The scene where the main character sobs stays in my memory.
She held her friend and sobbed.

examples.ko: 가족들이 아무 말도 못 하고 오열하고 있었어요.
examples.en: The family couldn't say anything and was sobbing.

explain: '울다'보다 훨씬 격하게, 목이 메어 흐느끼는 느낌이에요. 뉴스나 소설에서 많이 나오고, 일상에서는 '펑펑 울다'처럼 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It feels much more intense than '울다', like sobbing with a choked voice. It appears in news and novels, while in daily talk people often say '펑펑 울다'.

examples.en: In summer I eat oiji soaked in water.
Grandmother made the oiji herself.
Seasoned oiji is a good side dish for rice.
There is still some oiji left in the fridge.
I sliced the oiji thinly and rinsed it in water.

examples.ko: 입맛 없을 때 오이지에 찬물을 부어 먹어요.
examples.en: When I have no appetite, I pour cold water over oiji and eat it.

explain: 오이를 짭짤하게 절인 반찬이라 보통 썰어서 물에 헹궈 무침으로 먹거나 찬물에 담가 먹어요. 여름 밥상에 자주 올라오는 반찬이에요.
explain_en: It is cucumber pickled salty, so it is usually sliced and rinsed, then eaten as a seasoned side dish or soaked in cold water. It is a common side dish on summer tables.

examples.ko: 너무 매운 걸 먹었더니 오장육부가 뒤집히는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I ate something too spicy and my insides feel like they're turning over.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 국물을 마시니 오장육부가 풀리는 느낌이에요.
examples.en: Drinking warm soup makes my whole body feel relaxed.
My stomach hurts so much that my insides are twisting.
They say you live long if your internal organs are strong.
I was so startled I thought my insides dropped.
Oriental medicine clinics see the internal organs as the basis of health.

explain: 몸속 장기 전체를 가리키는 말이에요. 의학 설명에서는 '내장'이나 '장기'라고 하고, 일상에서는 '오장육부가 뒤틀리다/뒤집히다'처럼 속이 몹시 아프거나 불편할 때 써요.
explain_en: It refers to all the organs inside the body. Medical explanations use '내장' or '장기', while in daily talk it appears in '오장육부가 뒤틀리다/뒤집히다' when your insides hurt or feel awful.

examples.en: They lost their child, so how frightened they must have been.
To cry like that, how hard it must have been.
Having failed the exam, how upset must she be?
Living alone in a strange place, he must be so lonely.
How urgent it must have been for him to run off like that.

examples.ko: 아침도 못 먹고 일했으니 오죽이나 배고팠겠어요.
examples.en: He worked without breakfast, so he must have been so hungry.

explain: 뒤에 '-겠어요', '-ㄹ까요'가 와서 상대의 힘든 처지를 헤아릴 때 써요. '오죽'이나 '오죽하면'도 비슷하게 써요.
explain_en: It is followed by '-겠어요' or '-ㄹ까요' when you imagine how hard someone's situation is. '오죽' and '오죽하면' are used in a similar way.
